record.original_question: Suppose x: M -> E^m is a k-type immersion with spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, and let E_i be the subspace of E^m spanned by {x_i(p) : p in M}. Classify the 2-type immersions for which the subspaces E_1 and E_2 are linearly independent.

evidence.quote: Let x : M -> E^m be a k-type isometric immersion whose spectral decomposition is given by (1.1). Denote by E_i the subspace of E^m spanned by {x_i(p), p in M} (i in {1, . . . , k}). The immersion x (or the submanifold M) is said to be linearly independent if the subspaces E_1, . . . , E_k are linearly independent.
Problem 8. Study and classify linearly independent 2-type immersions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $x : M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold $M$ into Euclidean $m$-space. The immersion $x$ is said to be of finite $k$-type if its position vector admits a spectral decomposition
$$x = c + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $c \in \mathbb{E}^m$ is a constant vector and $x_1, \ldots, x_k : M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ are non-constant smooth maps satisfying $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for pairwise distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_k$ of the Laplace operator $\Delta$ of $M$ (with the sign convention $\Delta f = -\operatorname{div}(\nabla f)$ on functions, extended componentwise to vector-valued maps).

For each $i \in \{1, \ldots, k\}$, let $E_i \subset \mathbb{E}^m$ denote the linear subspace spanned by the set $\{x_i(p) : p \in M\}$. The immersion $x$ (equivalently, the submanifold $M$) is called linearly independent if the subspaces $E_1, \ldots, E_k$ are linearly independent, i.e.\ their sum is direct.

Problem. Classify all linearly independent $2$-type isometric immersions $x : M \to \mathbb{E}^m$; that is, determine all submanifolds $M$ of Euclidean space whose spectral decomposition has the form $x = c + x_1 + x_2$ with $\Delta x_1 = \lambda_1 x_1$, $\Delta x_2 = \lambda_2 x_2$, $\lambda_1 \ne \lambda_2$, and such that the subspaces $E_1$ and $E_2$ are linearly independent.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of classifying linearly independent 2-type immersions is listed among open problems on finite-type submanifolds, with partial results known (e.g., for hypersurfaces, spherical submanifolds, and immersions with geodesics of 2-type) but no complete classification appears to have been established. Surveys on submanifolds of finite type continue to list this as an outstanding classification problem.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Submanifolds: A Survey (B.-Y. Chen)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of linearly independent immersions and finite-type submanifolds, with classification results in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of linearly independent 2-type immersions in general remains an outstanding problem; only partial results in special settings are known.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems and conjectures on submanifolds of finite type: recent development
status_evidence.snippet: A survey of open problems concerning submanifolds of finite type, including problems on linearly independent immersions.
status_evidence.claim: The general classification of linearly independent 2-type immersions is listed among open problems.
